page: Microsoft Azure F8s_v2 is an FSv2-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, which aligns with compute-optimized hardware profiles. It includes 66 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates that the F8s_v2 delivers average performance across most compute and memory metrics. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance falls into the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 415.54 GB/sec and large block uncached memory reaching 47.24 GB/sec. The server demonstrates average capabilities in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

The F8s_v2 presents a tradeoff between compute density and memory capacity, offering a lower memory-to-vCPU ratio that reduces cost for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.4 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 2877.83 on Passmark. It also supports basic machine learning tasks, processing 447.5 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model.
description: Microsoft Azure F8s_v2 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine from the FSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and 66 GB of local storage. The hardware configuration delivers a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio, making it suitable for compute-focused workloads. Benchmark results place the server in the average tier for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though single-core stress-ng performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. The F8s_v2 is appropriate for web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations where high memory capacity is not a primary requirement.
